Class ForyCodecFactory

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.codec.fory.ForyCodecFactory
All Implemented Interfaces:
CodecFactory
public class ForyCodecFactory extends Object implements CodecFactory
A CodecFactory backed by Apache Fory: fast binary serialization for JVM-to-JVM payloads such as cache entries, queue messages and journal records.

Class registration is mandatory. Fory refuses to serialize or deserialize a class that has not been registered, which is what closes the deserialization-gadget class of attacks. This factory never relaxes that: build the ThreadSafeFory with requireClassRegistration(true) (the library default, and what of(Class[]) does) and register every type a codec will carry, including the element types of collections.

The wire format is Fory's own and JVM-specific. It is the right choice when Java is on both ends and speed and size matter; it is the wrong choice for anything another language will read, or for data that must outlive the classes that wrote it — use a schema-based or JSON backend for those.

Codecs must be thread-safe, and a plain Fory is not, so this factory accepts only a ThreadSafeFory — which is what of(Class[]) builds, and what Fory.builder()...buildThreadSafeFory() gives a caller who configures their own.

create(TypeRef) fails fast: if the instance requires registration and the requested type — or any class named in its type arguments — is not registered, it throws IllegalArgumentException at creation rather than letting the first encode fail in production. The check walks declared generics (List<Person> checks Person); it cannot see types that only appear at runtime inside registered classes' fields, which Fory itself still rejects.

    • of

      public static ForyCodecFactory of(Class<?>... classes)
      Creates a factory over a new thread-safe Fory instance, in Java mode with class registration required, with the given classes registered. Register every type a codec will carry — records, beans, and the element types of the collections they hold; the JDK's collections and boxed types are registered by Fory itself.
      Parameters:
      classes - the classes codecs from this factory may serialize
      Returns:
      a factory ready to create codecs for the registered classes

    • supports

      public boolean supports(Class<?> type)
      Reports whether this factory's Fory instance will serialize values of the given class. True when registration is not required; when the class is registered; or when the class is not something Fory serializes by its own identity — a JDK type, an interface, or an abstract class — because Fory registers the JDK's concrete types itself and decides interfaces and abstract types by the runtime class of each value.
      Parameters:
      type - the class to check
      Returns:
      whether codecs from this factory can carry values declared as that class
